summary: Demo capture docs cover the contract, workflow install, request, every outcome and reason, data exposure and local reproduction, consistent across policy, ADR, README and spec
basis: Read docs/policies/documentation.md (no project documentation policy exists). Compared the new Demo capture section of templates/policies/spec-kit-workflow.md with demo.py and run.py: contract limits, refusal reasons and remedies, exit codes, the output line format, the state table against demo.REASONS, resolve and lines, the stale, not-yet-requested, not-configured and configuration-invalid lines, and the 124/137 note. FR-019, AC-007 and AC-009 are covered: seeded nonsensitive data, video readable with repository read access, reproduce command named, changed command flagged. The README, TECHNICAL-SPEC 9.1, ADR-0013 (new, proposed, earlier ADRs untouched), ledger-schema.md, the run.py usage and the template header describe the same model. No screenshot applies. Two residual points are low/info and open. Same-provider review.

findings.label: implementation-bug
findings.reason: The policy says a refusal or GitHub failure dispatches and records nothing, which holds. An unexpected local error after a successful dispatch, such as a failed ledger append, also prints failed-retryable (internal-error) and exits 1 although a run was dispatched. That run is never linked or shown as captured. Name this case or give it a distinct reason. Fixed in 1b0cc91: the policy names a local error after a successful dispatch.

findings.label: spec-ambiguity
findings.reason: The README's copy-once section does not say ballast-demo.yml must be on the default branch before feature branches are cut. The policy section and the template header say it, and the README links the template, so this is a discoverability nit only. Fixed in 1b0cc91: the README entry says to commit the workflow on the default branch before cutting feature branches.
